book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Brief visits have their drawbacks

parts.note: brief and short are synonyms
visits are arrivals, comings

explanation.surface: Short calls on someone come with downsides.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortcomings are faults or failings, the same thing as drawbacks or weak points.

clue.text: Brief account of involvement with press difficulties

indicators.note: involvement suggests things getting tangled together, so the letters are mixed up with one another

parts.note: AC is the short form of account
taken as written

explanation.surface: A short report on someone's dealings with the newspapers turns into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief account' reads like a news summary, but it is just the abbreviation AC, mixed with the letters of press.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapes are awkward fixes or predicaments one gets into, a common informal word for troubles.

clue.text: Too much up above

definitions.meaning: second meaning: literally higher than the highest point of something

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for excess is also a plain description of a position above the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something excessive or exaggerated, and literally describes a position higher than the summit.

clue.text: Restrained on arrival when there's a chap around

indicators.note: the chap is placed around the other word, so it sits wrapped inside him

parts.note: Ted is a common man's name
once you have arrived, you are there

explanation.surface: Someone is held back the moment they arrive because a man is lurking.
explanation.walkthrough: The chap's name goes around the word for having arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A tethered animal is tied up by a rope, so held back or restrained in its movement.

clue.text: Where to work after skating?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a workplace with desks

definitions.note: read as two words, OFF ICE
definitions.meaning: second meaning: split into two words, where a skater is once finished on the rink

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as OFF ICE: after skating you are off the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is the room or building where desk staff do their jobs each day.

clue.text: Island of some national importance

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is used, the letters sitting inside it

parts.note: the middle four letters of this word

explanation.surface: An island said to matter to the whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides, famous for its abbey; 'importance' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small Hebridean isle off the coast of Mull in western Scotland.

clue.text: Possibility of sharing the decoration

indicators.note: a possibility is one of several ways things could go, so a possible rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps the ornaments could be split between people.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnish is an ornamental trimming added to a dish of food to make it look attractive.

clue.text: Could it identify one produced by instalments?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a code stamped on a manufactured item to tell it apart
second meaning: a single issue of a story published in parts

explanation.walkthrough: The identifying code on a product, read another way, is one issue of a story published in parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the unique code on a manufactured item, and also one issue (a number) of a story told in episodes.

clue.text: Listener at home being serious

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens
a bird's home is its nest

explanation.surface: Someone who listens quietly at home is a grave sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest describes a sincere, grave and intent manner, not joking or frivolous.

clue.text: Enjoyment has real unsuitability on a sad occasion

indicators.note: something unsuitable is not right as it stands, so the word must be put into a different order

parts.note: fun is enjoyment
these four letters reordered

explanation.surface: Having a good time would be truly out of place at a mournful event.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral is the ceremony for burying or cremating the dead, a mournful gathering.

clue.text: Where the hoi polloi learn to get depressed?

definitions.text: Where the hoi polloi learn to get depressed?

parts.note: surface reading: the common people, the masses
setter's reading: lessons in which you are taught to sink lower

explanation.walkthrough: The common people are the bottom tier of society; read literally, they are lessons in lowering, where one learns to be depressed (pushed down).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the usual name for the bottom social tier, the masses, which is what hoi polloi means.

clue.text: Give Tam nice pie cooked in haste

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hurriedly hands a Scot named Tam a pleasant pie straight from the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: Tam is a Scottish form of Thomas; 'Give' only sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatience is restless eagerness, wanting things done quickly, which shows itself as hurry or haste.

clue.text: Compete at the point where there's something to see

parts.note: to vie is to compete
a compass point, west

explanation.surface: Contestants battle it out at a spot with a sight worth seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a sight or vista, the scene before your eyes from some vantage spot.

clue.text: Speculate over ground for association with Alice

definitions.note: a phrase pointing to the answer rather than a synonym

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the first word sits on top of the second

parts.note: to wonder is to speculate
land is ground

explanation.surface: Musing on the reason for a link with someone named Alice.
explanation.walkthrough: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland is Lewis Carroll's children's classic.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonderland is the fantasy realm Lewis Carroll's heroine visits after falling down the rabbit hole.

clue.text: Incline to take a Frenchman back, one hears

parts.note: a ship that lists leans over

indicators.note: back tells us the name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: Leaning towards bringing a French fellow home again, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one hears' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A listener is a person who hears, an audience member paying attention to sounds or speech.

clue.text: Not dressed for putting up a fight

indicators.note: in a down clue putting up means lifting the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a war is a fight

explanation.surface: Stripped off, ready to scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not dressed' fits both bare skin and uncooked food or untreated wounds; here it is the undressed sense of a raw state.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw food has not been prepared with a dressing or cooking, and a raw wound is unbandaged.

clue.text: The two express hesitation when there's trouble

parts.note: both means the two
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A pair start hemming and hawing when problems arise.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother is fuss, nuisance or difficulty, a mild word for problems or annoyance.

clue.text: No sense going back to cause a hold-up

indicators.note: going back means the word runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: someone with no sense is mad

explanation.surface: Pointless retreating would only create a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is a barrier across a river which holds up the flow of water behind it.

clue.text: Tries to get a break after a short time in government

definitions.note: describes a person with a post in government

indicators.note: a break smashes something, so the word's letters fall into a fresh order

parts.note: MIN is the abbreviation for minute
these five letters reordered

explanation.surface: An official tries for a holiday after a brief spell in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the reworked letters behind the short time.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the cabinet who heads a department, so someone serving in the governing body.

clue.text: Result of firing into the air

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as two words, a shot sent skyward

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as UP SHOT for the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An upshot is the final outcome or consequence of events, so a result.

clue.text: Man at university adopts a different air as military man

indicators.note: a different version of the word means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Sam is a common man's name
U is the standard abbreviation for university
these three letters reordered

explanation.surface: A student takes on a new manner and plays the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of Japan's hereditary warrior class, a fighting man.

clue.text: To take a blow and go down could be a stroke of luck

parts.note: wind is what blows
to fall is to go down

explanation.surface: Getting hit and tumbling over might turn out to be fortunate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' tempts you into the boxing picture, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall is unexpected money or good fortune, originally fruit blown down from a tree.

clue.text: Is there when a race finishes

parts.note: taken as written
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
finishes means ends

explanation.surface: Someone turns up at the end of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to be present at it, to be in the room or at the place.

clue.text: Get about with some success at last when given a break

definitions.note: cryptic: what a doctor does for a broken bone

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning
to get something somewhere is to set or put it there

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone gets around and finally does well after a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a fractured bone is what gets reset, so 'given a break' is the cue rather than a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon resets a fractured bone, putting it back into position after it has been broken.

clue.text: Hobo quietly making contact

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A tramp silently gets in touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump is a knock or collision, a moment of physical touching between two things.

clue.text: Runs down to dine out where there are fires

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: these four letters reordered
coal fires burn in grates

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at eating out in places with open hearths.
explanation.definitionFit: To denigrate is to belittle or disparage, to criticise unfairly, which is to run something down.

clue.text: Flow of hot water?

parts.note: surface reading: steaming water pouring from a tap or spring
setter's reading: a Scottish stream, or the injury scalding water gives

explanation.walkthrough: A burn is the Scots word for a stream, a flow of water, and also what very hot water can give you.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a small stream is called a burn, and scalding water causes a skin injury of the same name.

clue.text: Find another way about outer diversion

indicators.note: a diversion sends something off its usual course, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning
these five letters reordered

explanation.surface: Drivers seek an alternative road around a ring-road detour.
explanation.definitionFit: To reroute is to send traffic or travellers along a different path or course.

clue.text: One learns to fall in where one drives off

indicators.note: in says one word is put inside the other

parts.note: in golf you drive off from the tee
rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: A golf novice learns to stand in line at the first hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall in' looks like the military order to line up; 'fall' is the weather and 'in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is a person being taught a job or skill, someone still learning.

clue.text: Side starting out making great progress

indicators.note: out means set out of place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A team beginning its campaign moves forward fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant strides is an idiom for rapid advances or big steps forward in development.
